A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GausSim study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulation experiments on READY and synthetic Bunny, including quantitative comparisons, efficiency measurements, ablations, and qualitative appendix examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds SSIM and LPIPS results in appendix Tables A4–A5.

M1.justification: The continuum-mechanics simulator, CMS hierarchy, physics constraints, training losses, network architecture, and interactive-force procedure are retained. Writing the network as ψθ clarifies its parameterization without changing the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use READY's Mothorchids, Carnation, Pudding, and Duck, plus synthetic Bunny. Long-term prediction, multiple-view rendering, joint training, and interactive examples are retained. The added metrics reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: DreamGaussian4D (DG4D) and PhysDreamer (PD) remain the evaluated external baselines. The new SSIM/LPIPS tables use the same comparator set, and membership in the existing efficiency and ablation comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and new Appendix A4.4 add SSIM and LPIPS evaluation alongside ℓ2 error. The reported training budgets, preprocessing, seen/unseen splits, and baseline evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The mass and momentum ablations, joint-training analysis, hierarchy efficiency comparison, multiple-view examples, and interactive pudding demonstration are retained. Tables A4–A5 add benchmark measurements without introducing a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: The existing ± reporting practice is retained and reused in Tables A4–A5. v3 adds no explanation of its statistical meaning, run or seed counts, confidence-interval procedure, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Tables A4–A5 add complementary SSIM and LPIPS results for the retained experiments, with GausSim leading every reported column. For example, its unseen Mothorchids scores are SSIM 0.990 and LPIPS 0.0247. Existing ℓ2, efficiency, and ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions and appendix derivations are retained. Equation 2 changes '=' to '≈', matching the first-order approximation already explicitly stated in v2. The prediction-count formula is equivalently reformatted; other changes concern notation and numbering.

C1.justification: Both versions claim realistic elastic simulation through continuum mechanics, an efficient CMS hierarchy, explicit mass and momentum constraints, and the READY dataset. The added metric results support these existing claims without changing their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of dissipation-related evaluation shortcuts, physics-constraint effects, and joint training retain their meaning. The limitations involving motion blur, segmentation noise, and Gaussian reconstruction quality are also retained despite shortened wording.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising a future code/model release to reporting their availability through the linked project page. The appendix's architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, and baseline implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to Physically Compatible 3D Object Modeling from a Single Image, UbSoft, and TopoGaussian, extending its examples of robotics and reconstruction applications. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording and notation clarifications, updates an author affiliation, adds acknowledgements, and inserts Appendix A4.4 for SSIM/LPIPS evaluation. The main section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables A4–A5, relocates Table 1 and Figure A2, and presents the prediction-count formula inline. Captions and text placement receive small adjustments. All existing figure imagery is retained.

improvement.justification: Tables A4–A5 strengthen v2's ℓ2-based quantitative evaluation with complementary structural and perceptual measurements on the same experiments. Notation clarifications and the updated code/model access statement also improve usability. These are limited gains: the scientific scope, original results, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
